validation.notes.value: Version-specific review dated 2026-09-27. The current bioRxiv version is v3, posted 2026-08-03, with title “Combining brain-wide activity imaging with electron microscopy reveals a distributed brain network for processing threatening somatosensory stimuli”; version 2 (2026-03-19) is titled “Combining brain-wide activity imaging with electron microscopy reveals a distributed nociceptive network in the brain,” matching the title in the Europe PMC JATS. bioRxiv v3 reframes the context as threatening somatosensory input involving nociceptive and mechanosensory pathways. The whole-brain neural assay nevertheless uses optogenetic activation of Basin interneurons in an extracted first-instar nervous system, followed by eFIB-SEM of that same specimen; the Basin manipulation does not isolate physical noxious versus mechanical input. v3 retains 119 responsive neurons and 25 lineages, and specifies that 26/50 selected neurons were traceable at intermediate branches. Its separate early-third-instar behavioral assay combines optogenetic Basin activation with Kenyon-cell inactivation and reports reduced rolling plus increased turning (366 experimental and 351 control larvae); these behaviors are distinct endpoints, not direct pain measures. This title/version proposal intentionally leaves the existing method, dataset, performance, limitations, and their field-resolution entries unchanged because those mechanistic extractions are explicitly sourced to the Europe PMC v2 JATS. The v3 article-info/full-text responses were captured as HTTP 200 in the same-day owner-source pass; a fresh request during this review returned HTTP 429, so the archived same-day official response was used. Europe PMC continues to serve JATS article-version 2; its v2 text is retained as the locator for existing extracted fields.
